tables.name: closed_deals
tables.description: Leads that became sellers (won deals). One row per deal, keyed by mql_id (joins to leads). seller_id joins to sellers with a LEFT JOIN: many deal sellers never sold anything, so revenue from funnel sellers covers only those with orders. Deals recorded as won before the lead's first contact are excluded as data errors.

columns.name: mql_id
columns.description: Lead that became this deal. Primary key; join: closed_deals.mql_id = leads.mql_id.

columns.name: seller_id
columns.description: Seller account created from the deal. LEFT JOIN to sellers: many deal sellers never sold anything, so they are not in sellers.

columns.name: sdr_id
columns.description: Sales development rep who qualified the lead. Anonymized id; no names available.

columns.name: sr_id
columns.description: Sales rep who closed the deal. Anonymized id; no names available.

columns.name: won_at
columns.description: When the deal was won.

columns.name: days_to_close
columns.description: Days from the lead's first contact to the deal being won.

columns.name: business_segment
columns.description: Seller's market segment, e.g. home_decor, health_beauty. Different from products.category.

columns.name: lead_type
columns.description: Kind of business, e.g. online_medium, online_big, industry, offline.

columns.name: behaviour_profile
columns.description: Personality profile (cat, eagle, wolf, shark) or a combination like 'cat, wolf'. Use ILIKE '%wolf%' to include combinations.

columns.name: business_type
columns.description: Seller's business type: reseller, manufacturer, other. NULL if not recorded.

columns.name: declared_monthly_revenue
columns.description: Monthly revenue in BRL as self-reported by the seller. NULL if not declared (most deals).

tables.name: customers
tables.description: One row per real customer. Home address = most common address among their last 3 orders, ties broken by most recent. For where a specific order went, use orders.delivery_*.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Unique person id (Olist customer_unique_id). Count this for number of customers.

columns.name: zip_prefix
columns.description: 5-digit zip prefix of the home address, as text with leading zeros.

columns.name: city
columns.description: Home city, lowercase without accents, e.g. sao paulo.

columns.name: state
columns.description: Two-letter Brazilian state code of the home address, e.g. SP, RJ. Preferred field for area questions.

tables.name: geolocation
tables.description: One row per 5-digit zip prefix: its city and state. Some customer/seller zips are missing here, so LEFT JOIN.

columns.name: zip_prefix
columns.description: 5-digit zip prefix as text with leading zeros, e.g. 01037. Join from customers.zip_prefix, sellers.zip_prefix or orders.delivery_zip_prefix with a LEFT JOIN.

columns.name: city
columns.description: Most common city for this zip prefix, lowercase without accents, e.g. sao paulo.

columns.name: state
columns.description: Two-letter Brazilian state code for this zip prefix, e.g. SP, RJ.

tables.name: leads
tables.description: Marketing qualified leads (MQLs): businesses that asked to become sellers on Olist. One row per lead. A lead CONVERTED if its mql_id appears in closed_deals; conversion rate = closed deals / leads. Covers 2017-06-14 to 2018-05-31 only.

columns.name: mql_id
columns.description: Unique lead id (MQL = marketing qualified lead, anonymized). Join: closed_deals.mql_id = leads.mql_id.

columns.name: first_contact_date
columns.description: Date the lead first contacted Olist (date only, no time).

columns.name: landing_page_id
columns.description: Anonymized id of the signup landing page. No page names or URLs are available.

columns.name: channel
columns.description: Marketing channel the lead came from: organic_search, paid_search, social, direct_traffic, email, referral, display, other, other_publicities, unknown.

tables.name: order_items
tables.description: One row per UNIT sold. There is no quantity column: buying 3 of a product = 3 rows. Units = COUNT(*). Revenue = SUM(unit_price), excluding orders with status canceled or unavailable. Count orders from the orders table, not here (some orders have no items).

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Order this unit belongs to. Join: order_items.order_id = orders.order_id.

columns.name: item_number
columns.description: Position of this unit within the order (1, 2, 3...). Not a unique id; the key is (order_id, item_number).

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: Product sold. Join: order_items.product_id = products.product_id (for category).

columns.name: seller_id
columns.description: Seller of this unit. One order can contain items from several sellers.

columns.name: ship_by_at
columns.description: Deadline for the seller to hand this item to the carrier.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: Price of one unit in BRL, excluding shipping.

columns.name: freight
columns.description: Shipping cost for this unit in BRL. 0 means free shipping.

columns.name: item_total
columns.description: unit_price + freight: what the customer paid for this unit including shipping.

tables.name: order_payments
tables.description: One row per payment; an order can have several (e.g. voucher + credit card). Use for HOW customers pay. Revenue comes from order_items, not here. NEVER join order_payments and order_items in the same query without first aggregating each to one row per order_id, or totals are multiplied.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Order this payment is for. Join: order_payments.order_id = orders.order_id.

columns.name: payment_number
columns.description: Position of this payment within the order (1, 2, 3...). Key is (order_id, payment_number).

columns.name: method
columns.description: Payment method: credit_card, boleto (Brazilian bank slip), voucher, debit_card, unknown.

columns.name: installments
columns.description: Number of instalments the payment was split into (e.g. 10 monthly payments). Not an amount. NULL if invalid.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Total amount of this payment in BRL (not per instalment). Sum per order for total paid.

tables.name: order_reviews
tables.description: Customer satisfaction reviews. One review can cover several orders and one order can have several reviews; key is (review_id, order_id). For average score, use WHERE is_latest_for_order so each order counts once. NEVER join with order_items or order_payments without aggregating each to one row per order_id first.

columns.name: review_id
columns.description: Review (survey answer) id. Not unique on its own: one review can cover several orders. Key is (review_id, order_id).

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Order reviewed. Join: order_reviews.order_id = orders.order_id. An order can have several reviews; filter is_latest_for_order to count each order once.

columns.name: score
columns.description: Satisfaction score from 1 (worst) to 5 (best).

columns.name: title
columns.description: Optional review title, in PORTUGUESE. NULL if empty.

columns.name: message
columns.description: Optional review comment, in PORTUGUESE. NULL if empty. Keyword searches must use Portuguese words.

columns.name: sent_at
columns.description: When the satisfaction survey was sent to the customer.

columns.name: answered_at
columns.description: When the customer answered the survey.

columns.name: is_latest_for_order
columns.description: True for the most recently answered review of each order. Filter on this for per-order averages and counts.

columns.name: has_comment
columns.description: True if the customer wrote a title or a comment.

tables.name: orders
tables.description: One row per order. For delivery questions, filter status = 'delivered' and exclude has_date_issue. Date columns are NULL when the order has not reached that stage.

columns.name: order_id
columns.description: Unique order id. Count this for number of orders. Join: order_items / order_payments / order_reviews.order_id = orders.order_id.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: The real person who placed the order. Join: orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Order status: delivered, shipped, canceled, unavailable, invoiced, processing, created, approved.

columns.name: purchased_at
columns.description: When the customer placed the order (Brazil local time). Never NULL. Use this for orders or revenue by day, month or year.

columns.name: approved_at
columns.description: When payment was approved. NULL if never approved (e.g. cancelled before payment).

columns.name: shipped_at
columns.description: When the order was handed to the carrier. NULL if not shipped yet or cancelled.

columns.name: delivered_at
columns.description: When the customer received the order. NULL if not delivered yet, cancelled, or lost.

columns.name: estimated_delivery_at
columns.description: Delivery date promised to the customer at purchase (date only, stored as midnight Brazil time). Never NULL. is_late compares delivered_at with this.

columns.name: delivery_zip_prefix
columns.description: 5-digit zip prefix the order was delivered to, as text with leading zeros. LEFT JOIN to geolocation (some zips are missing there).

columns.name: delivery_city
columns.description: City the order was delivered to, lowercase without accents, e.g. sao paulo.

columns.name: delivery_state
columns.description: State the order was delivered to. Use this for orders-by-area questions; customers.state is the customer's home.

columns.name: delivery_days
columns.description: Days from purchase to delivery. NULL if not delivered.

columns.name: is_late
columns.description: True if delivered after the estimated delivery date. NULL if not delivered.

columns.name: has_date_issue
columns.description: True for impossible date combinations; exclude these from delivery-time analysis.

tables.name: products
tables.description: One row per product. Product NAMES ARE NOT AVAILABLE (removed by anonymization): identify products by product_id and category only, never invent names.

columns.name: product_id
columns.description: Unique product id (anonymized). The only way to identify a product; there are no product names.

columns.name: category
columns.description: Product category in English, snake_case, e.g. health_beauty, bed_bath_table. 'unknown' if missing. A few untranslated categories keep their Portuguese name.

columns.name: name_length
columns.description: Number of characters in the product name. The name itself is not available.

columns.name: description_length
columns.description: Number of characters in the product description. The description itself is not available.

columns.name: photo_count
columns.description: Number of photos on the product listing.

columns.name: weight_g
columns.description: Package weight in grams. NULL if missing.

columns.name: length_cm
columns.description: Package length in centimetres. NULL if missing.

columns.name: height_cm
columns.description: Package height in centimetres. NULL if missing.

columns.name: width_cm
columns.description: Package width in centimetres. NULL if missing.

columns.name: volume_cm3
columns.description: Package volume in cubic centimetres (length x height x width). NULL if any dimension is missing.

tables.name: sellers
tables.description: One row per seller on the Olist marketplace. Join to order_items for sales. Sellers acquired through the marketing funnel appear in closed_deals.seller_id (LEFT JOIN: not every deal has a seller here).

columns.name: seller_id
columns.description: Unique seller id (anonymized; no seller names available). Join: order_items.seller_id = sellers.seller_id.

columns.name: zip_prefix
columns.description: 5-digit zip prefix as text with leading zeros. LEFT JOIN to geolocation (some zips are missing there).

columns.name: city
columns.description: Seller city, lowercase without accents, e.g. sao paulo. State suffixes removed; invalid values replaced from geolocation.

columns.name: state
columns.description: Two-letter Brazilian state code, e.g. SP. Preferred field for seller-area questions.

joins.note: Some customer zips are missing from geolocation.
Some seller zips are missing from geolocation.
Some delivery zips are missing from geolocation.
Many deal sellers never sold anything, so they have no row in sellers.

data_facts.note: Period covered by orders. 'This year', 'last month', 'recently' are anchored to the latest date here, not today's date. Nothing exists after it.
Period covered by the marketing funnel (leads and closed deals). Funnel questions outside it have no data.
